sections.title: What is the LIC Jeevan Utsav Plan (Plan 771)?

content.text: LIC Jeevan Utsav (Plan 771) is a non-linked, non-participating whole-life savings plan with a limited Premium Paying Term (PPT). The two headline features are:

items: Guaranteed Additions (GAs) during the PPT — calculated at ₹40 per ₹1,000 Basic Sum Assured per year.
Lifetime income after PPT — choose Regular Income (a fixed 10% of Basic Sum Assured per year) or Flexi Income (defer and accumulate income at a guaranteed ~5.5% p.a.).

content.text: This makes Jeevan Utsav attractive when you want a guaranteed, post-PPT income stream without market risk.

sections.title: How the LIC Jeevan Utsav Plan Calculator Works

content.text:
Inputs

Age, Basic Sum Assured (BSA), Premium Paying Term (5–16 years), income option (Regular/Flexi), payment mode (Yearly/Half-Yearly/Quarterly/Monthly) and any optional riders.

Core calculations

items: Annual premium — calculated from LIC rate tables (we apply standard modal loadings to show half-yearly, quarterly & monthly equivalents).
Guaranteed Additions (GAs) — formula: GA per year = (BSA / 1000) × 40. GAs are added at each policy year-end only during PPT.
Regular Income — after PPT: Income = 10% × BSA per year, paid for life.
Flexi Income — unclaimed income accrues at 5.5% p.a. compounded; you can withdraw a portion per LIC rules (the calculator shows accumulated pool and withdrawal options).
Death benefit — higher of Sum Assured on Death or 105% of total premiums paid (sum assured on death is defined in the brochure; often the higher of BSA or 7× annualized premium).
GAs total (over PPT) = GA per year × PPT = (BSA / 1000) × 40 × PPT
Regular Income = 0.10 × BSA every year after PPT.
Flexi pool after N years (accumulating) = future value of an annuity: Income × (((1+r)^N − 1) / r), where r = 0.055 (5.5%).

sections.title: Worked Examples from Our LIC Jeevan Utsav Calculator

content.text:
Example 1 — Early planner (Age 30, BSA ₹10L, PPT 12, Regular)

Inputs: Age 30, BSA ₹10,00,000, PPT 12 years, Regular Income.

Annual premium (illustrative): ₹85,500 × 12 years → Total premiums paid = ₹85,500 × 12 = ₹10,26,000.

Guaranteed Additions: GA per year = (10,00,000 / 1000) × 40 = ₹40,000. Over 12 years: ₹40,000 × 12 = ₹4,80,000.

Post-PPT income: Regular income = 10% × 10,00,000 = ₹1,00,000 per year for life (paid annually).

Example 2 — Mid-career (Age 40, BSA ₹20L, PPT 10, Flexi)

Inputs: Age 40, BSA ₹20,00,000, PPT 10 years, Flexi Income.

Annual premium (illustrative): ₹2,10,000 × 10 years → Total premiums = ₹21,00,000.

GAs: GA per year = (20,00,000 / 1000) × 40 = ₹80,000. Over 10 years: ₹80,000 × 10 = ₹8,00,000.

Flexi income after PPT = 10% × 20,00,000 = ₹2,00,000 per year. If you defer withdrawals for 5 years (i.e., do not withdraw the ₹2L each year for 5 years), the accumulated pool is:

FV of annuity = Income × (((1+0.055)^5 − 1) / 0.055)

Compute: (1.055^5 ≈ 1.305 → (1.305 − 1) = 0.305). So FV = 200,000 × (0.305 / 0.055) = 200,000 × 5.545 ≈ ₹11,09,000 (approx).

Plus accumulated GAs (₹8,00,000) → total illustrative pool ≈ ₹19.09 Lakh after 5 years of deferral.

Example 3 — Pre-retirement (Age 50, BSA ₹15L, PPT 8, Regular + rider)

Inputs: Age 50, BSA ₹15,00,000, PPT 8, Regular Income, AD&DB rider costing ≈₹2,000 extra/yr (illustrative).

Base premium: ≈ ₹2,50,000/yr. With rider: ≈ ₹2,52,000/yr for 8 years → Total paid ≈ ₹2,52,000 × 8 = ₹20,16,000.

GAs: GA per year = (15,00,000 / 1000) × 40 = ₹60,000 → total GAs over 8 years = ₹4,80,000.

Income after PPT: 10% × 15,00,000 = ₹1,50,000 per year for life.

Example 4 — Flexi pool illustration (BSA ₹10L, PPT 12): how the ~₹17.7L number is built

This is a common question: you’ll often see a “Flexi pool ≈ ₹17.7L” figure for a ₹10L policy with PPT 12 and a 10-year deferral. Here's the exact arithmetic:

  1. Regular income each year after PPT = ₹1,00,000.
  2. If you defer withdrawals for 10 years, the future value of yearly ₹1,00,000 payments at 5.5% is:
    FV = 100,000 × (((1.055)^10 − 1) / 0.055).
  3. Compute (rounded): (1.055^10 ≈ 1.708). So (1.708 − 1) = 0.708.
  4. FV = 100,000 × (0.708 / 0.055) = 100,000 × 12.8727 ≈ ₹12,87,270.
  5. Now add the Guaranteed Additions accrued during PPT: for PPT 12, GAs total = ₹40,000 × 12 = ₹4,80,000.
  6. Total accumulated pool ≈ ₹12,87,270 + ₹4,80,000 = ₹17,67,270 → rounded ≈ ₹17.7 Lakh.

That’s why many examples show ~₹17.7L — it’s the sum of accumulated deferred incomes (FV) plus total GAs.

Example 5 — Large cover (Age 35, BSA ₹1 Crore, PPT 10 — quick snapshot)

Large BSA examples scale linearly. If BSA=₹1,00,00,000 and PPT=10:

  • GA per year = (1,00,00,000 / 1000) × 40 = ₹4,00,000 per year → total GAs (10 years) = ₹40,00,000.
  • Regular income = 10% × 1,00,00,000 = ₹10,00,000 / year for life.

Example 6 — Quick surrender vs paid-up (conceptual)

If you stop paying premiums after 3 years, you typically have a surrender/paid-up decision. Paid-up reduces SA proportionally but keeps vested GAs; surrender gives a cash value (guaranteed or special). Our calculator shows both numbers so you can compare—always run the calculator with your exact dates for precise figures.

sections.title: Jeevan Utsav vs Jeevan Umang vs New Jeevan Anand

rows: Lifetime income after PPT (Regular 10% BSA / Flexi)

items: Entry age: from 90 days (completed) to 65 years (varies by product rules).
Premium Paying Terms: 5 to 16 years (your PPT choice affects GA totals & income start).
Riders: AD&DB, Accident Benefit, Term Assurance, Critical Illness, Premium Waiver — they raise premium but give extra cover.
Loan / Surrender: Loan available after the policy gains surrender value (usually after 2 premiums); surrender value or paid-up values vary — always verify with LIC for exact figures.
Income and death benefits can be tax-exempt under Section 10(10D) subject to conditions (e.g., premium-to-SA ratios).
GST is applied on premium; commonly ~4.5% in first year and ~2.25% thereafter (confirm at purchase).

sections.title: Jeevan Utsav Plan Calculator: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

items.a: The Guaranteed Additions and the 10% Regular Income rule are defined in the product document — they are guaranteed per the product (non-linked, non-participating). For illustration use official LIC brochure (UIN 512N363V02).

Regular gives immediate predictable income (10% BSA/yr). Flexi is best if you want to accumulate and potentially withdraw larger sums later — it grows at 5.5% p.a. If you need steady annual cash, choose Regular.
GAs accrue only during the Premium Paying Term (PPT). After the PPT they stop; income begins as per your chosen option.
Jeevan Utsav’s core design is lifetime income after PPT. It’s not a lump-sum maturity product; however, accumulated Flexi pools and GAs produce a sizable value which you can withdraw per LIC rules.
Higher of Sum Assured on Death or 105% of total premiums paid; SAD definition per brochure.
Yes, after policy acquires value; terms per LIC.
They add protection; they do not change GA or the 10% income rule.

conclusion.title: Conclusion: A Lifelong Income Stream for a Secure Future

content.text: LIC's Jeevan Utsav is a powerful tool for anyone seeking a guaranteed, lifelong income stream after a limited premium payment period. Whether you choose the predictable 'Regular Income' or the flexible 'Flexi Income' option to grow your wealth, this plan is an excellent choice for creating a secure, lifelong financial legacy. It's best suited for individuals looking for a reliable, non-market-linked income stream in their post-retirement years, combining savings and protection in one powerful package.

mainEntity.name: What are Guaranteed Additions in Jeevan Utsav?

acceptedAnswer.text: Guaranteed Additions accrue at ₹40 per ₹1,000 Basic Sum Assured at the end of each policy year during the Premium Paying Term only.

mainEntity.name: What is Regular vs Flexi Income?

acceptedAnswer.text: Regular Income pays 10% of Basic Sum Assured annually for life after PPT. Flexi Income allows you to defer income; unclaimed income accrues at 5.5% p.a. compounded and you can withdraw part of the accumulated pool.
The death benefit is the higher of the Sum Assured on Death or 105% of total premiums paid up to date of death, subject to product terms.
